corrected_value.authors: Miller MW; Kaloupek DG; Dillon AL; Keane TM
corrected_value.title: Externalizing and internalizing subtypes of combat-related PTSD: A replication and extension using the PSY-5 scales

decisions.quote: A LPA was conducted on the higher-order temperament traits PEM, NEM, and CON, which yielded support for a 3-class solution. These three classes reflected internalizing, externalizing, and simple subtypes of posttraumatic response, replicating prior cluster analytic work ( Sellbom & Bagby, 2009 ; Miller et al., 2003 , 2004 ; Miller & Resick, 2007 ). As with prior studies, NEM, PEM, and CON distinguished between the classes, with the internalizing subtype marked by high NEM (particularly Stress Reaction) and low PEM, while the externalizing class was marked by high NEM and low CON.
decisions.reason: Wolf et al. (2012) empirically re-test the three-class personality typology of posttraumatic psychopathology (internalizing characterized by high NEM/low PEM, externalizing characterized by high NEM/low CON, and simple PTSD with normal-range traits) using latent profile analysis in 208 veterans with PTSD symptoms (Aim 1, line 10; Results, lines 16-19) and explicitly conclude in the Discussion (line 20) that their three-class solution replicates the prior cluster-analytic work of Miller, Kaloupek, Dillon, & Keane (2004). Full bibliographic identity is verified in the reference list (lines 56-57: Miller MW, Kaloupek DG, Dillon AL, Keane TM, 2004, Journal of Abnormal Psychology, 113, 636-645, DOI 10.1037/0021-843X.113.4.636). This is an independent empirical study using MMPI-2 PSY-5 scales in combat-related PTSD and is not a duplicate report, wave, or alternate version of the sole shipped row 58 (Miller, Greif, & Smith, 2003, Psychological Assessment, 10.1037/1040-3590.15.2.205). Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent.

corrected_value.title: Internalizing and externalizing subtypes in female sexual assault survivors: Implications for the understanding of complex PTSD

decisions.location: Discussion, line 22 (also Introduction Aim 2, line 10; Discussion, line 20; reference at lines 58-59)
decisions.quote: Cluster B PD features were more prevalent among the externalizing class while features of schizoid and avoidant PD were more prevalent in the internalizing class. This replicates initial work in this area ( Miller & Resick, 2007 ), but provides stronger evidence for these associations because of improvements in the measurement of PD and in the analytic approach used in this study.
decisions.reason: Wolf et al. (2012) explicitly design Aim 2 (line 10) to re-test the Axis II personality disorder (PD) comorbidity patterns across the three PTSD personality subtypes originally reported by Miller & Resick (2007)—specifically that externalizers endorse more Cluster B PD features while internalizers score highest on schizoid and avoidant PD—and also include Miller & Resick (2007) among the three-class cluster-analytic studies replicated in Aim 1 (line 20). In the Discussion (line 22), the authors explicitly state that their IPDE interview findings replicate Miller & Resick (2007). Full bibliographic identity is verified in the reference list (lines 58-59: Miller MW, Resick PA, 2007, Behavior Therapy, 38, 58-71, DOI 10.1016/j.beth.2006.04.003). Miller & Resick (2007) studied female sexual assault survivors using the SNAP and is an independent study completely distinct from the sole shipped row 58 (Miller, Greif, & Smith, 2003, 10.1037/1040-3590.15.2.205). Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent.
